episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a CNC Machinist / Programmer — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: A quiet stretch: mostly you and the work. Human contact in this job is the exception, not the rule — long solo runs are the normal texture of the day. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: A message lands: could you also take on one more thing today — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you?

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Hands-on time. You make, fix or adjust the real thing in front of you — the part of the job you can touch, and the part where skill is visible. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Lighting the Roaster
episodes.text: You arrive in the cool roastery and walk to the roaster. You set the temperature and time controls for the first batch. You light the burner and start the conveyors and blower.

trial.title: Start the roaster right
items: Start the conveyor and blower
Light the roaster burner
Set the time control
Set the temperature control
trial.explain: You set temperature and time first, then light the heat, then start the moving equipment.

episodes.title: Watching the Gauges
episodes.text: You sit down by the gauges and watch temperature and pressure. You check them again and write nothing down. It is the same as yesterday and will be the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Checking the Beans
episodes.text: You scoop a few hot beans and rub them between your fingers. You smell them and look at the color. You taste one to check it matches the standard.

episodes.title: Taking Lab Samples
episodes.text: You pull a small sample of roasted beans into a bag for the lab. You hold the warm bag and look at the roast. You decide how to handle it before the next batch.

choice.prompt: The sample looks uneven — do you take it now or take a fresh one after mixing?

options.label: Send this bag as is
options.outcome: You seal and label the bag and it goes to the lab. The result comes back for this exact scoop.

options.label: Mix and take a fresh sample
options.outcome: You stir the batch, scoop again, and send that bag. The lab tests the more even mix.

episodes.title: Roaster Jam
episodes.text: You hear the conveyor stutter and see beans pile up at the inlet.

choice.prompt: You cleared it once and it still jams — try again or call it in?

options.label: Try one more adjustment
options.outcome: You stop the feed and clear the jam again. The flow restarts and you keep watching it closely.

options.label: Notify your supervisor now
options.outcome: You call your supervisor over to the roaster. They take over the machine while you stand back.

chat.text: Hear that grinding? Flow stopped?
Try to clear it once, but don’t force it.

episodes.title: Holding the Roast Steady
episodes.text: You look at the humidity gauge and the bean sample side by side. You turn the thermostat valve down a little. You watch until the readings hold steady again.

episodes.title: Morning Task Brief
episodes.text: You arrive at the dock and sit with the crew for the day's job. You listen for what the dive task is and what the water and weather are doing. You ask a couple of plain questions before anyone suits up.

trial.title: What to check first
trial.scenario: You are told the dive task and hear the tide is running fast and the visibility is poor. Your air and standby plan depends on those conditions.
options: Ask for the latest water current and visibility before planning the dive
Skip the conditions and start suiting up right away
Plan only for yesterday's conditions
trial.explain: You need the task and the current conditions first to plan safely.

episodes.title: Gear Check Again
episodes.text: You sit on the bench and go through your helmet, mask, air tank, harness, and gauges. You check each strap and reading the same way you did yesterday. Same checks tomorrow.

episodes.title: Signing In Ashore
episodes.text: You stand at the small office and register the dive with the authorities. You write down the planned depth and time limit. You clip that plan to your board for the day.

episodes.title: Down the Ladder
episodes.text: You pull on the suit and scuba gear while two helpers hold you steady. You step backward down the ladder and feel the cold come up. You give the helpers a nod and let yourself sink.

choice.prompt: Your helper asks if you are ready to drop below the surface chop or hold on the ladder a moment longer.

options.label: Drop now with helpers holding the line
options.outcome: You descend steady while they manage your line and you reach work depth.

options.label: Hold on the ladder for another minute
options.outcome: You wait, breathe, and then descend once the surge eases.

episodes.title: Talking Up the Line
episodes.text: You are on the bottom and keep your hand on the signal line.

chat.text: Topside here, how is your air and depth?
Give us a pull on the line and talk on the phone.
Copy, we have you at your time mark.

episodes.title: Time Called Early
episodes.text: You feel fine but topside calls that you are near your planned depth and time limit. You know the safety rule is to respect length and depth. You start to wrap the task.

choice.prompt: You are close to finishing and must decide about your dive length and depth limit right now.

options.label: Start up now and stay inside the limit
options.outcome: You ascend slowly and log the dive as planned.

options.label: Stay a few more minutes to finish
options.outcome: You push past the limit and topside logs an overrun to review.

options.label: Ask topside for a clear call on time and depth
options.outcome: Topside confirms your numbers and talks you up step by step.

episodes.title: Morning Sketches
episodes.text: You arrive at your desk and open yesterday's notes for a new kitchen tool. You sit down with your computer-aided design equipment. You start rough sketches of ideas for the handle shape.

episodes.title: Check With Engineering
episodes.text: You walk to a small meeting room to confer with engineering and marketing about the concept.

choice.prompt: Engineering wants a thicker shape, marketing wants it thin. How do you settle the concept now?

options.label: Agree to test a slightly thicker shape
options.outcome: You sketch the thicker version and engineering confirms it can be made.

options.label: Keep the thin shape for now
options.outcome: You keep drawing, but you note the production risk to check later.

chat.text: Production says that thin handle will crack in the mold.
Marketing still wants it to look light and simple. What do you think?

episodes.title: Checking What Works
episodes.text: You sit back down to evaluate the two handle ideas for feasibility. You compare appearance, safety, function, and serviceability. You check budget and production costs and methods against what the market expects.

trial.title: Spot the feasilbility risk
trial.scenario: You review your handle design. It looks good and feels good in your hand. The wall is too thin to mold safely at the planned budget.
options: The wall thickness fails safety and production cost
The color looks outdated for the market
The sketch lines are too light to read
trial.explain: The thin wall breaks safety and production limits at this budget.

episodes.title: Refining The Model
episodes.text: You spend the middle of the day modifying the working model to match the specs. You adjust the same curves and edges again. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Approval Meeting Turns
episodes.text: You stand with the customer and design committee to present your designs and report.

choice.prompt: The committee will not approve the design as shown. What do you offer in the room?

options.label: Offer to refine the design to their specs
options.outcome: They list two spec changes and you agree to bring back updated drawings.

options.label: Ask to keep the design and explain your reasons
options.outcome: They listen, then still ask for modifications to meet production limits.

options.label: Ask which change matters most for approval
options.outcome: They point to the handle strength and you agree to fix that first.

chat.text: We cannot approve this. It does not meet our specs and looks dated.
We need a change before we sign off. What can you do?

episodes.title: Updating The Drawings
episodes.text: You are back at your desk with your drafting tools and design software. You modify and refine the detailed drawings to match what the customer asked for. You clean up the illustrations so production can read them clearly.

episodes.title: Renewals List Again
episodes.text: You arrive and sit down at your desk. You open the same renewal spreadsheet as yesterday. You check dates and mark the ones still waiting.

episodes.title: Finding New Names
episodes.text: You sit with your notebook and work through yesterday's contacts. You add a few new businesses to your prospect list. You plan who to call next for new business.

choice.prompt: You have an hour free. How do you look for new clients?

options.label: Call back referrals from current clients
options.outcome: You call two referrals. One answers and agrees to meet next week.

options.label: Visit new businesses on Main Street
options.outcome: You stop in at three shops. Two take your card and one asks for a quote.

episodes.title: Walking Through Policies
episodes.text: You sit down with a small business owner at your table. You lay out two property policies side by side. You explain what each one covers and what it leaves out.

trial.title: Explain the trade-off
trial.says: Just tell me straight — what's good and bad about this property policy?
options: This one costs less but covers less for fire damage, this one costs more and covers more.
This one is the best plan and has no downsides for you.
Just sign here and we will sort the details later.
trial.explain: You name both the advantage and the disadvantage so the buyer can decide.

episodes.title: Building the Package
episodes.text: You work on a program for a farm client. You pull together auto, property, and crop coverage into one plan. You adjust the limits to fit what they actually run.

episodes.title: Coverage Gap Call
episodes.text: You get a call from a client who needs proof of coverage today.

choice.prompt: The client needs broader coverage by tomorrow. What do you do?

options.label: Customize the program now to add the missing risk
options.outcome: You rework the policies and send updated proof. The client has coverage for the job.

options.label: Renew the current policies as they are
options.outcome: You process the renewal unchanged. The job site still flags the gap.

options.label: Set a meeting next week to review options
options.outcome: You book a time to talk through policies. The client still has no proof for tomorrow.

chat.text: We have a job tomorrow and they say our auto and property coverage is not enough.
Can you fix this today?

episodes.title: Filing the Day
episodes.text: You sit back at your desk to close out sales. You update the records for today's policies and renewals. You file the forms so tomorrow starts clean.

episodes.title: Preflight System Check
episodes.text: You arrive at the plane in the early light. You walk around it and climb into the cockpit. You check the engines, controls, instruments, and other systems one by one. Everything has to read right before you go.

trial.title: Order the preflight check
items: Check the instruments in the cockpit
Check the engines for proper function
Check the other aircraft systems
Check the flight controls
trial.explain: You work from engines to controls to instruments, then the rest of the systems.

episodes.title: Takeoff Speed Math
episodes.text: You sit down with the numbers for this airport. You factor in the altitude, the outside temperature, the plane weight, and the wind speed and direction. You work out the speed you need to become airborne.

choice.prompt: The wind direction just shifted on the report. What do you do?

options.label: Recalculate the takeoff speed now
options.outcome: You run the numbers again with the new wind. You update the takeoff speed before taxi.

options.label: Keep the first number and go
options.outcome: You stay with the old speed. You roll with a number that no longer fits the wind.

episodes.title: Watching The Gauges
episodes.text: You settle into cruise and watch the same gauges. You check engine operation, fuel flow, and the systems lights. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Sharing The Controls
episodes.text: You are in the right seat for this leg. Your co-pilot flies while you back them up.

chat.text: I have the controls for climb-out.
Can you watch engines and fuel while I fly?
Call out if anything drifts off.

episodes.title: Clouds Close In
episodes.text: The clouds thicken ahead and the ground drops away. Visibility goes poor fast. You shift to your instruments to keep the plane steady.

choice.prompt: Visibility is gone outside. What do you trust now?

options.label: Fly by instruments and monitor systems
options.outcome: You keep your eyes inside and fly the gauges. You stay steady until you see outside again.

options.label: Keep looking outside for a gap
options.outcome: You stare into the grey for a break. You fall behind the instruments while the plane keeps moving.

episodes.title: Steady Systems Watch
episodes.text: You are back in clear air on the last stretch. You scan engine operation and fuel consumption again. You check that the aircraft systems are still working as they should.

episodes.title: Morning Blood Pressure Table
episodes.text: You arrive at the community center and set up the blood pressure cuff and sign-in sheet. You greet each person and check their blood pressure one by one. You write down each reading for the nurse to review.

episodes.title: Talking Through Screening Options
episodes.text: You sit down with a small group waiting for screening information.

choice.prompt: The group looks unsure and time is short. What do you cover first?

options.label: Explain what each screening checks for
options.outcome: You walk through breast screening, pap smears, and diabetes checks in plain words. They ask a few questions and take the clinic flyer.

options.label: Help the overdue woman schedule first
options.outcome: You sit with her and call the clinic to book her breast screening. The rest of the group waits and you talk with them next.

chat.text: I missed my last breast screening. Do I still need to go?
Pap smears and diabetes checks confuse me.
They have questions about what each screening is for.

episodes.title: Same Cuff Same Chairs
episodes.text: You sit back at the same table with the same cuff. You check blood pressures again, name after name. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Afternoon Immunization Line
episodes.text: You move to the side room for the immunization clinic. You prepare the basic preventive shots and call people in order. You give each immunization and watch them for a few minutes after.

trial.title: Nervous About the Shot
trial.says: I am scared of shots. Do I really need this one?
options: You do not need it if you do not want it, just leave.
This preventive shot helps keep you from getting sick, and I can talk you through what will happen.
Everyone else did it with no problem, so you should too.
trial.explain: The professional reply gives clear information about prevention and offers support.

episodes.title: Worried Talk About Home
episodes.text: You meet with a client to talk about staying safe from domestic violence. She becomes quiet and says she does not feel safe at home right now. You stay calm and listen.

choice.prompt: She says she is afraid to go home tonight. What do you do now?

options.label: Stay with her and review safety options
options.outcome: You stay with her and talk through safe places she can go and who she can call. You offer to connect her to local support services.

options.label: Give her information to take home
options.outcome: You give her written information about domestic violence resources and safe contacts. You note your concern and ask if you can follow up tomorrow.

options.label: Ask if she wants help contacting support
options.outcome: You ask permission and then help her call a support line from your office. You sit with her while she talks to them.

episodes.title: Updating Client Files
episodes.text: You sit at the desk and open today's client records. You add plans, notes, and forms from the screenings and talks. You check that each file is complete before you leave.

episodes.title: Morning Written Test
episodes.text: You arrive at the testing room early. You lay out the written forms in rows. You check each applicant's ID before they sit down.

episodes.title: Oral Questions Begin
episodes.text: You sit across from an applicant for the oral test. You read the next question from your list.

chat.text: Sorry, I'm nervous. Can you repeat that?
I think the answer is to stop and check first.
Did I get that part right?

episodes.title: Taking License Fees
episodes.text: You sit at the counter collecting license fees. You take the same payment and print the same receipt. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Handing Out Licenses
episodes.text: You check the list of applicants who met the standards. You pull their approved forms to issue licenses. One file is missing a final signature.

choice.prompt: One file that met standards is missing a final signature. What do you do?

options.label: Hold the license until it is signed
options.outcome: You set the license aside. You tell the applicant to return once the signature is complete.

options.label: Issue the license anyway
options.outcome: You hand over the license. You note the file is incomplete and will need fixing later.

episodes.title: Checking Shop Walls
episodes.text: You walk into a small shop for a visit. You scan the wall where the permit should be displayed. You check the date and standards on what you find.

trial.title: Find What Is Wrong
trial.scenario: You visit a shop to check licenses on the wall. Two permits are current and clearly displayed. The third permit expired two months ago.
options: The two current permits on display
The expired permit on the wall
The color of the frames
trial.explain: The expired permit no longer meets licensing standards and needs attention first.

episodes.title: Warning About Violation
episodes.text: You return to a shop with no valid license on display. You tell the owner this breaks licensing standards. You explain the penalty that can follow.

choice.prompt: The owner has no valid license displayed. How do you warn them?

options.label: Give a spoken warning and a deadline
options.outcome: You warn the owner in person. You give a clear date to fix the license display.

options.label: Write the warning on the visit form
options.outcome: You write down the infraction and penalty. You hand the owner a copy to keep.

episodes.title: Morning Problem Review
episodes.text: You log in and open the problem log. You read through a hardware slowdown and a software error side by side. You start mapping where the two issues overlap.

episodes.title: Network Health Check
episodes.text: You sit down and run the same network checks as yesterday. You confirm hardware, software, and availability step by step. You log that everything is steady, same as tomorrow will be.

episodes.title: Vendor Call Together
episodes.text: You join a call with your manager and a vendor about a fix that is stuck.

choice.prompt: The vendor asks for system time and your manager waits on you. What do you offer?

options.label: Offer a short joint test window
options.outcome: You set a one-hour window together. You watch the test and note what holds.

options.label: Ask to postpone a week
options.outcome: They agree to wait. You keep the current workaround running until then.

chat.text: We need their cooperation to move this forward this week.
Our update can solve it, but we need time on your system.
What do you think we should offer them?

episodes.title: Testing A New Use
episodes.text: You sit with a familiar computing principle. You try adapting it to a small new use. You test it, watch where it bends, and adjust.

trial.title: Adapt a principle
items: You test the adapted principle on a small example
You review the principle behind the current method
You adjust the adaptation and try again
You note where it breaks for the new use
trial.explain: You first review the principle, then test it small before you adjust and note results.

episodes.title: Network Goes Down
episodes.text: You see alerts that part of the network is unavailable to users. You check hardware and security measures for the cause. You need to act to bring access back.

choice.prompt: Users are waiting and the cause is unclear. What do you do first?

options.label: Isolate the affected section and restore access
options.outcome: You reroute users to the stable section. Availability returns while you keep digging.

options.label: Run a deeper check before changing anything
options.outcome: You hold the network as is. You gather logs for ten more minutes before you act.

episodes.title: Planning Tomorrow Tasks
episodes.text: You look at work priorities and goals for the week. You assign small tasks and set their order for tomorrow. You send the schedule out to the team.

episodes.title: Catching Up on Chips
episodes.text: You arrive at your desk and open your laptop. You read a short update about new microprocessors and support logic. You jot down two changes you need to remember for your work.

episodes.title: Talking Through the Specs
episodes.text: You sit down with two engineers to review the specifications.

choice.prompt: The software need and the hardware spec do not quite line up. What do you do next?

options.label: Walk through the specs together line by line
options.outcome: You find the mismatch in the interface timing. You agree on a small hardware change to test.

options.label: Ask for a short break to recheck requirements
options.outcome: You come back with the performance notes marked. The group picks one requirement to clarify first.

chat.text: The software team needs faster response from the support logic. Can the current board handle it?
Check the interface notes with them before we change anything.

episodes.title: Sketching the New Board
episodes.text: You sit at your computer and work on your CPU board design. You adjust the layout for the custom integrated circuits. You save a clean version to prototype later.

trial.title: Prototype Build Order
items: Test the working model with computer simulation
Modify the prototype after testing
Build a working model of the design
Review test results to find fixes
trial.explain: You build first, then test, then review, then modify.

episodes.title: Same Test Again
episodes.text: You sit at the bench with the disk drive prototype. You run the same simulation test as yesterday. You log the same readings, same as tomorrow.

episodes.title: Prototype Stops Working
episodes.text: You start the simulation on your working model and it fails. The board does not respond the way the model predicted. You pause and look at the test readout with the team.

choice.prompt: The prototype failed the test. What do you do first?

options.label: Rebuild the working model and test again
options.outcome: The second test fails the same way. You set the model aside for a closer check of the build.

options.label: Change one part of the design and retest
options.outcome: You modify the support logic section. The next simulation runs a little longer before stopping.

options.label: Stop and compare the model to the spec
options.outcome: You spot a missed interface detail. You mark it to fix in the next build.

episodes.title: Writing Down the Details
episodes.text: You return to your desk and open the hardware notes. You write the functional specification for today's build and test changes. You save it so the team can follow the introduction steps.

episodes.title: Checking Last Night's Backup
episodes.text: You sit down and open the backup log. You see last night's backup finished. You check the added and deleted files list.

trial.title: Find the backup problem
trial.scenario: Three shared folders backed up overnight. Two show complete. One shows no new copy since two days ago.
options: The folder with no new copy for two days
A folder that backed up fine last night
A folder with one small file added
trial.explain: The missed backup needs attention first before it falls further behind.

episodes.title: Coordinating the Upgrade
episodes.text: You join a call to coordinate today's maintenance and upgrade.

chat.text: Are we still doing the maintenance this afternoon?
Yes, if the repair window stays open. Can you coordinate the order?

episodes.title: Recommending a Firewall Fix
episodes.text: You sit down with the results of a network security audit. You see a gap in the firewall rules. You draft what to recommend next.

choice.prompt: The audit shows an open rule you did not expect. What do you recommend?

options.label: Recommend closing the rule now and running an automated probe
options.outcome: You close the rule and start the probe. You watch the results come in to check nothing else is exposed.

options.label: Recommend leaving it and rechecking in the next audit
options.outcome: The rule stays open for now. You note it for the next audit and move on to other work.

episodes.title: Clearing Old Files
episodes.text: You open the file queue. You add the new files and delete the old ones marked for removal. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Network Goes Down
episodes.text: Part of the network stops responding and messages start coming in.

choice.prompt: The problem is still unclear. What do you do first?

options.label: Roll back the last change to restore connection
options.outcome: You roll back the change. The connection returns and you log what failed.

options.label: Test a new fix on the live network
options.outcome: You apply a small fix. You stay with it to see if the connection holds.

chat.text: Users in one area lost connection. Can you look?
Let me know what solution you are trying first.

episodes.title: Writing Recovery Steps
episodes.text: You open the disaster recovery plan draft. You write down the steps to recover files from backup. You save the updated plan for the team.

episodes.title: Checking Overnight Systems
episodes.text: You arrive and log in at your desk. You open the monitoring dashboard to test last night's program install. You watch the status lines to make sure everything is still running.

trial.title: Order the install check
items: Run a test on the installed program
Confirm the system keeps monitoring normally
Coordinate the install time with users
Install the program on the system
trial.explain: You coordinate first, then install, then test, then monitor.

episodes.title: Helping With Login Problem
episodes.text: You sit down with your headset on. A staff member messages you about a program problem.

chat.text: Hi, my program keeps freezing when I try to open it.
I restarted but it still will not load.
Can you walk me through what to check?

episodes.title: Midmorning System Checks
episodes.text: You run the same tests on the same programs. You log that everything is still working. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Looking At Inventory Costs
episodes.text: You sit at your computer after lunch. You pull up production and inventory numbers to look at costs. You compare how the data moves between the two systems.

choice.prompt: The cost numbers do not match the inventory numbers. What do you dig into first?

options.label: Trace the inventory data flow
options.outcome: You follow the inventory records step by step and find where the count splits off.

options.label: Rebuild the cost summary first
options.outcome: You rerun the cost analysis and see the same gap, so you still need the inventory side.

episodes.title: System Goes Down
episodes.text: You get an alert that a system has stopped working. You open the error logs to see the malfunction. People are waiting for it to come back.

choice.prompt: The system is down and users are waiting. What do you do first?

options.label: Isolate the failing program
options.outcome: You stop the failing program and the rest of the system starts responding again.

options.label: Restart the whole system
options.outcome: You restart everything and it comes back up, but you still do not know what failed.

options.label: Ask users to wait and keep checking
options.outcome: You keep watching the logs while users wait, and the system stays down longer.

episodes.title: Linking Two Systems
episodes.text: You sit back at your desk. You work on linking two office systems so they can share information. You check that the same record looks the same on both sides.

episodes.title: Walking The Forms
episodes.text: You arrive before the truck. You walk the line of forms and crouch to sight down them. You check each joint and brace to see they are properly built.

episodes.title: Setting Pitch And Depth
episodes.text: You loosen the stakes and tap the side forms up and down. You set them to pitch and depth and pull the string to align them. You lock them back down and check again.

episodes.title: Raking And Smoothing
episodes.text: You shovel and rake the pour across the forms. You pass the screed, then the float, then the trowel. Same pass as yesterday, same pass tomorrow.

episodes.title: Cutting Joints And Edges
episodes.text: You kneel at the slab edge with your hand tools. You mold the edge straight and cut the expansion joint line. You run the straightedge along it to check your work.

trial.title: Find The Bad Joint
trial.scenario: You run the straightedge over two fresh joints. One joint is straight and even. The other joint is wavy and the edge is slumping.
options: The wavy joint and slumping edge need attention first
The straight joint needs attention first
Both joints are fine and need nothing
trial.explain: The wavy joint and edge will not hold shape unless fixed now.

episodes.title: Wind Drying The Slab
episodes.text: The afternoon wind picks up hot across the fresh slab.

choice.prompt: The wind is drying the concrete too fast while you watch it cure. What do you do?

options.label: Slow down and keep checking the cure
options.outcome: You pause the trowel and watch the surface. You catch the dry spots early and keep the finish even.

options.label: Keep smoothing without pausing
options.outcome: You keep working the surface. The top dries while you finish and small cracks start to show.

chat.text: Feel that? Surface is drying fast.
You seeing cracks at the edge?

episodes.title: Finishing Beside Crew
episodes.text: You work the float down the slab beside another finisher. You level and smooth your side to match his. You both check the surface as the heat holds.

choice.prompt: Your section is still rough but his side is ready for edging. What do you do?

options.label: Stay on your float and finish leveling
options.outcome: You stay back and get your surface flat. You join him at the edge a few minutes later.

options.label: Stop floating and start edging with him
options.outcome: You move to the edge too soon. Your side stays uneven and you have to go back over it.

options.label: Ask him to help float your side first
options.outcome: He comes over and you both level your side. You move to edging together when it is ready.

episodes.title: Morning Blueprints
episodes.text: You arrive and open the plans on your screen. You measure rooms and count materials. You start a list for time, cost, and labor.

episodes.title: Yesterday's Numbers
episodes.text: You open the same cost file you use every day. You copy in past material and labor rates. It is the same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Call About Changes
episodes.text: You sit with the revised drawing up. Your phone rings about a wall change.

choice.prompt: The wall moved and your material count is now off. What do you do?

options.label: Recalculate now and explain the change
options.outcome: You adjust the materials and labor and send the new total. The record stays clear.

options.label: Keep the old estimate to save time
options.outcome: You leave the old numbers in place. The bid no longer matches the plans.

chat.text: We moved that interior wall two feet. Does that change your numbers?
Can you update the estimate today?
Let me know what you need from me.

episodes.title: Checking Actual Costs
episodes.text: You sit down with the bid and the costs so far. You compare what you planned to what was actually spent. You note where the project is over and under.

trial.title: Spot the overrun
trial.scenario: You track actual costs against the bid. Labor is close to plan. One material line is well above what you bid.
options: Ignore it and check again next month
Flag the material cost that is over bid
Rewrite the whole bid from scratch
trial.explain: You flag the line that is over bid so the gap is clear.

episodes.title: Tender Deadline Slip
episodes.text: You check the tender list and a subcontractor price is missing. The deadline is close and you cannot finish without it. You need to decide how to keep the process moving.

choice.prompt: A key subcontractor price is missing before the tender closes. What do you do?

options.label: Call and ask for the price now
options.outcome: You get a number or a no-bid answer. You can close the tender with real information.

options.label: Submit the tender without that price
options.outcome: You send an incomplete tender. The total is missing a real cost.

options.label: Extend the deadline for everyone
options.outcome: You notify all bidders of more time. The process stays fair but runs late.

episodes.title: Filing The Tender
episodes.text: You sit and log today's bids and notes in the tender file. You save each version in the same place. You close the folder when everything matches.

episodes.title: The core work
episodes.text: You start the main work of a Content Strategist — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: People time
episodes.text: People need things from you — questions, help, decisions. You deal with them one at a time, the way this job always does. Real people, real reactions — this is the human side of the job, as it actually feels.

choice.prompt: Someone you're working with asks you to take on one more thing — extra work, on top of everything already in front of you today.

options.label: Say yes and fit it in
options.outcome: You fit it in. The day runs longer, the work gets done properly — and the person who asked remembers that you said yes.

options.label: Say no, politely
options.outcome: You say no, and you say why. A short, slightly awkward moment — then the rest of your day stays yours.

options.label: Offer a smaller version
options.outcome: You offer the part you can actually do, and by when. Most days that's accepted — saying yes to everything is how this job burns people out.

episodes.title: Hands on
episodes.text: Tools-and-systems time: you work the equipment and the screens of the trade until the thing in front of you does what it should. Skilled, hands-on work — the part where being good at it shows.

trial.title: The check-in
trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.
Honestly? Don't ask. It's a disaster.
trial.explain: The professional reply says where things stand and what happens next — short, honest, no drama.

episodes.title: The routine block
episodes.text: The same block as yesterday: the repeating tasks that never make the brochure. You do them again, carefully, because skipping them is exactly how mistakes happen. The same again tomorrow. This block repeats more than any other part of the job.

episodes.title: It goes wrong
episodes.text: Something goes wrong — it always does, some days. A problem lands on you that was in nobody's plan, and sorting it out is now your job. Unplanned and unavoidable — how the job feels when it pushes back.

episodes.title: The paperwork
episodes.text: End of day: notes, records, the write-up of everything you did. The work isn't finished until it's written down. Nobody's favourite part. It still has to be done, every day.

episodes.title: Checking Morning Numbers
episodes.text: You open yesterday's consumer survey and a short roundup of ad trends. You compare what people say about two similar products. You note which angle might promote yours best.

trial.title: Pick the lead
trial.scenario: You review trends and surveys for a soap ad. One chart shows buyers care most about price. A note says a competitor's funny ad is getting shared a lot.
options: Lead with the low price in the copy
Copy the competitor's joke word for word
Ignore the surveys and pick a theme you like
trial.explain: The surveys show price matters most to these buyers.

episodes.title: Building Campaign Together
episodes.text: You sit with the creative director and art director. You look at the blank layout for a new client together.

chat.text: We need to decide how to present the price message.
I left space up top for a short headline.
What headline fits best with that picture?

episodes.title: Same Lines Again
episodes.text: You rewrite the same product line for email, then for a short ad, then for a web banner. You swap a word here and there to fit the tone for each medium. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Showing Drafts to Client
episodes.text: You sit down with the client on a video call. You walk through two draft headlines and the main idea. You wait while they read the words on the screen.

choice.prompt: The client frowns at the second headline. What do you do now?

options.label: Ask which words bother them
options.outcome: They point to two words they want changed. You write down their exact wording to use.

options.label: Move on to the next idea
options.outcome: You present the next draft. They ask to go back to the second one later.

episodes.title: Fixing Copy Fast
episodes.text: You get a message that the copy misses the mark. You join a quick call to talk through what must change.

choice.prompt: The client wants the middle paragraph changed today. What do you change first?

options.label: Rewrite the product claim in their theme
options.outcome: You send a new version that evening. They approve the claim and leave the rest for tomorrow.

options.label: Rewrite the whole ad from the top
options.outcome: You run out of time before the full rewrite is clean. You send a rough draft and they mark it up.

options.label: Keep the copy and explain your theme
options.outcome: They listen but still ask for the change. You agree to send a revised paragraph.

chat.text: This theme does not fit our product.
Can you change the middle paragraph today?

episodes.title: Talking Through Themes
episodes.text: You sit back with your notes on the product and the ad themes. You tighten a paragraph so the tone fits the medium better. You read it aloud to hear if it holds.

episodes.title: Sorting the Handouts
episodes.text: You arrive before anyone else and unlock the training room. You lay out the handouts in neat piles on each table. You check the visual materials against your list and replace a torn page.

episodes.title: Listening to Needs
episodes.text: You sit down with two warehouse workers for short interviews. You ask what parts of the job still feel shaky. You write down their answers about what help they need.

choice.prompt: They both say the new packing steps are confusing. You have ten minutes left. What do you ask next?

options.label: Ask for a specific example from yesterday
options.outcome: They walk you through a missed step. You note it for the next skills session.

options.label: Move on to your survey questions
options.outcome: You finish the list on time. You miss the detail about the packing steps.

episodes.title: Role Play Circle
episodes.text: You stand in front of twelve new hires for the morning session. You split them into pairs for a short role play about customer requests. You walk the circle and listen to each group discussion.

trial.title: Answering a doubt
trial.says: I don't see how this role play helps with my real job.
options: This is just how we do it here, so please keep going.
You are right, this is silly. We can skip it.
Pretend I am the customer from yesterday. What would you say first?
trial.explain: You link the exercise straight back to the real job task.

episodes.title: Same Skills Session
episodes.text: You run the same job skills practice you ran yesterday. You read through the same slides and the same exercise. You watch the same clock as the group works through it again.

episodes.title: Virtual Room Fails
episodes.text: You switch to the virtual session and the video freezes for half the group.

choice.prompt: The virtual room keeps freezing. Do you keep it virtual or switch modes?

options.label: Stay virtual with audio only and share the slides
options.outcome: You finish with audio and slides. The session runs long and feels flat.

options.label: Move the group to the in-person room downstairs
options.outcome: You gather everyone downstairs. You start late but finish the exercise face to face.

chat.text: Half of us lost video. We can only hear you.
Should we cancel or try phone only?
We still need this done today. What do you want to do?

episodes.title: Filing the Guides
episodes.text: You sit back at your desk with the training guides. You file the updated procedure manual and tidy the course folder. You log which handouts need reprinting for tomorrow.

episodes.title: Morning Station Wipe
episodes.text: You arrive and pull on your smock. You wipe down your station and chair. You sanitize your scissors and combs. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Fitting In Appointments
episodes.text: You sit at the front desk with the appointment book open.

choice.prompt: Two clients want the last Saturday morning slot. What do you do?

options.label: Book the first client and offer the second a weekday
options.outcome: The first client takes Saturday. The second sighs and books Thursday instead.

options.label: Put one on the waitlist for Saturday
options.outcome: You write one name in for Saturday. The other goes on the waitlist for a cancellation.

chat.text: Can I get Saturday morning? Any time works.
I need Saturday too. I can only do mornings.
We only have one spot left Saturday.

episodes.title: First Cut of Day
episodes.text: You drape the cape around your customer. You check her hair type and facial features as she explains what she wants. You cut and shape with scissors and clippers. You trim the edges clean with trimmers.

trial.title: Answering a cut request
trial.says: Can you trim it like this photo but leave it longer on top?
options: Got it, longer on top. I'll check the shape with you as I cut.
Sure, whatever, I'll just cut it short.
I don't do photos, just tell me inches.
trial.explain: You repeat back the instructions and check as you work.

episodes.title: Mixing Warm Brown
episodes.text: You pull on gloves and mix the brown dye. You brush it on section by section with the applicator brush. You set the timer and watch the color develop.

episodes.title: Color Moving Fast
episodes.text: You check the bleach and the hair is lifting faster than you expected. The ends look pale already. You need to decide right now.

choice.prompt: The bleach is processing fast. What do you do?

options.label: Rinse it out now
options.outcome: You rinse the bleach at the sink. The hair is light enough and you move on to tone it.

options.label: Leave it five more minutes
options.outcome: You wait and check again. The ends turn dry and you have to cut them shorter.

options.label: Ask a senior stylist to look
options.outcome: She comes over and checks a strand. She nods to rinse now and helps you at the sink.

episodes.title: Writing Down Today
episodes.text: You sit down with the customer cards. You write down the cut and color you did today. You file the records for tomorrow.

episodes.text: You start the main work of a Costume Designer — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

trial.says: Hey — how's that thing coming along that you were working on?
options: It's on track. I'll flag it straight away if I need help or it slips.
Fine.

episodes.title: Morning Walkaround
episodes.text: You arrive early and climb around the crane. You inspect the mechanisms and lifting accessories. You adjust one loose fitting so it holds steady.

episodes.title: Checking the Cable
episodes.text: You crouch by the drum and run your eyes along the cable. You check the grappling device for wear. You mark one worn section to replace.

trial.title: Find the wear
trial.scenario: You are inspecting the cable and grappling device before any lift. You see a smooth oiled cable, a clean hook latch, and one strand sticking up frayed. Only one of these needs attention first.
options: The frayed strand on the cable
The smooth oiled cable
The clean hook latch
trial.explain: A frayed strand means wear that can fail under load.

episodes.title: Setting the Outriggers
episodes.text: You stand by the crane as the helpers get the blocking ready. You point where each pad needs to go.

choice.prompt: The left outrigger blocking sits uneven. What do you do?

options.label: Have them reset the blocking
options.outcome: They pull it out and reset it level. You check it again before you move the crane.

options.label: Lift anyway and watch it
options.outcome: You stay off the levers. The lift waits until the blocking is reset and solid.

chat.text: Where do you want this blocking?
This left pad feels soft under here.

episodes.title: Weighing the Load
episodes.text: You look at the weight ticket for the next bundle. You check it against the lifting capacity chart in the cab. You confirm you are clear to lift.

episodes.title: Moving Loads Again
episodes.text: You sit in the seat and move the levers and foot pedals. You lift a load, swing it over, and set it down. Same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Heavy Load Warning
episodes.text: You check the next load weight and it sits right at your lifting limit. You hold off the controls. You know an overload is not worth the risk.

choice.prompt: The load weight is at your capacity limit. What do you do?

options.label: Refuse the lift and ask for a lighter load
options.outcome: You stay parked. The crew breaks the load into two lighter picks.

options.label: Check the chart again with a supervisor
options.outcome: You go over the weights and capacities together. You only lift if the numbers show you are clear.

episodes.title: Morning customer numbers
episodes.text: You sit down and open yesterday's customer data. You sort through demographics, preferences, and buying habits. You mark which groups bought and which stayed quiet.

episodes.title: Talking through research
episodes.text: You join a call with marketing and polling colleagues to compare notes on consumer opinions.

choice.prompt: The team asks what to research next. What do you focus on?

options.label: Look closer at unhappy buyers
options.outcome: You pull their comments and buying history. You bring three clear patterns back to the next call.

options.label: Look for a new market group
options.outcome: You filter the demographics for a group you have not served. You share the size and needs with the team.

chat.text: I saw your notes on buying habits. What are shoppers saying this week?
Do we need to change our questions for the next round?

episodes.title: Checking survey replies
episodes.text: You open the same satisfaction survey inbox you checked yesterday. You count the new replies and log them in the same sheet. It looks the same as yesterday, and will look the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Building the survey
episodes.text: You sit with a blank questionnaire about customer satisfaction. You write short questions and put them in a clear order. You check that each one asks for one thing only.

trial.title: Order the survey work
items: Send the questionnaire to customers
Decide what satisfaction question to answer
Write clear survey questions in order
Pick how to collect the answers
trial.explain: You decide what to learn first, then pick the method and write the questions before you send anything.

episodes.title: Missing satisfaction data
episodes.text: You open the satisfaction results and half the answers are missing. The deadline for your update is still today. You have to decide how to handle the gap.

choice.prompt: Half the satisfaction data is missing. What do you do?

options.label: Use existing past data for now
options.outcome: You pull last month's satisfaction answers to fill the gap. You note clearly what is old and what is new.

options.label: Fix the collection and wait
options.outcome: You fix the broken survey link and wait for fresh replies. Your update goes out late with complete data.

options.label: Report only what you have
options.outcome: You report the small set of replies you have. You explain the gap and how you will collect the rest.

episodes.title: Writing up findings
episodes.text: You turn today's findings into a short report with one simple chart. You write what the numbers mean in plain words. You save it for the team to read.

episodes.text: You start the main work of a Customer Success Manager — the core of the job, done properly, start to finish. No audience and no shortcut: this is the thing everything else in the day supports. This is the work the whole job is built around.

episodes.title: Morning Virus Check
episodes.text: You sit down and log in from home. You open the overnight reports of computer viruses. You scan them to see if anything affects your systems.

episodes.title: Same Protection Check
episodes.text: You check the virus protection system status. It shows the same version as yesterday. You confirm no update is needed and log the check. Tomorrow you will do it again.

episodes.title: Access Request Call
episodes.text: You see a new request about access. You open the computer security file to review it.

choice.prompt: The access change is waiting in the security file. What do you do?

options.label: Update the access now as asked
options.outcome: You change the access status and save the file. The old access is removed and the new access works.

options.label: Check the request details first
options.outcome: You pause and confirm the correct team and files. You then update the access status with the right details.

chat.text: Hi, I moved teams this week.
Can you remove my old file access and add the new team?
I still need the new files for today.

episodes.title: Locking the Transfer
episodes.text: You prepare a confidential file for transfer. You encrypt the data transmission. You check the firewall to keep out tainted transfers.

trial.title: Order the secure transfer
items: Send the file on its way
Erect the firewall to keep out tainted transfers
Encrypt the data transmission
Check that confidential information stays concealed
trial.explain: You encrypt first, then protect with the firewall, then check before sending.

episodes.title: Emergency Processing Failure
episodes.text: You see normal data processing has stopped. You open the emergency data processing plan. You see files at risk of modification and disclosure.

choice.prompt: The emergency plan is open and files are at risk. What do you do first?

options.label: Switch to emergency processing now
options.outcome: You start emergency processing. The files stay available while you work on the main system.

options.label: Lock the files from changes first
options.outcome: You block changes to safeguard the files. You then start emergency processing a few minutes later.

episodes.title: Updating the Plan
episodes.text: You sit down to update the safeguard plan. You add notes from today's risk assessment and test of the system. You save the plan to cover modification, destruction, and disclosure.

episodes.title: Morning Warm-Up Circle
episodes.text: You greet your morning group as they stretch by the barre. You explain the counts out loud, then you demonstrate the sequence slowly. Everyone tries it together while you keep time.

episodes.title: Watching Each Student
episodes.text: You send students across the floor in small groups. You watch closely for ability, limits, and interests. You note who is steady, who is straining, and who lights up.

trial.title: Who Needs Attention First
trial.scenario: Three students finish the across-the-floor phrase. One is steady but bored, one keeps smiling and trying, and one is wincing and favoring an ankle.
options: The student favoring an ankle
The steady but bored student
The smiling student trying hard
trial.explain: A physical limit or pain needs attention before boredom or effort.

episodes.title: Different Needs Same Room
episodes.text: You split the class for the next combination. You give one side a slower breakdown and the other side the fuller turn version. You change your words and demo to fit each group.

choice.prompt: One beginner looks lost while the advanced students get restless. What do you do now?

options.label: Keep everyone on the full version together
options.outcome: The beginner falls further behind and stops trying. You finish the hour with most of the room with you and one student quiet.

options.label: Give the beginner a simpler facing and counts
options.outcome: She stays in the dance with a version she can do. You cue both groups and keep the room moving.

options.label: Pair her with an advanced student to practice
options.outcome: They drill the basics in the corner while you lead the rest. You check in often and adjust as they go.

episodes.title: Same Basics Again
episodes.text: You run the afternoon beginners through the same basic positions. You count the same rhythm and correct the same posture. You repeat the drill again, just like yesterday and tomorrow.

episodes.title: Wanting To Quit
episodes.text: A teen stays after the hard combination class, frustrated and close to tears. You sit beside her on the floor.

choice.prompt: She wants to quit the challenging turn. What do you do?

options.label: Encourage her to stick with a smaller part
options.outcome: She agrees to keep working on the entry steps only. You set a short practice plan for next week.

options.label: Suggest a different beginner class to explore

episodes.text: You sit down at your desk and open the database architecture document. You add yesterday's changes to the diagrams and notes. You save a clear version so others can follow it.

episodes.title: Meeting With Architects
episodes.text: You join a video call with a system architect and a design analyst. They walk through what the business needs from the data. You take notes on what the database must support.

choice.prompt: They describe two business needs and you cannot cover both today. Which do you clarify first?

options.label: Ask about the reporting need
options.outcome: You stay on the call and map what data the reports need. You leave with a clear list to design from.

options.label: Ask about the storage limit
options.outcome: You stay on the call and pin down how much data must be kept. You write the limit into your design notes.

episodes.title: Checking the Notes
episodes.text: You go back over the same architecture notes again. You fix the same small labels and formatting. It looks the same as yesterday and will look the same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Planning in Stages
episodes.text: You sit with the business requirement and plan the strategy in stages. You sketch the modeling idea, then the design, then how you will implement it. You keep each stage simple and linked to the requirement.

choice.prompt: The application is timing out for users. What do you do first?

options.label: Check the data partitions and indexes
options.outcome: You look at the partitions and indexes and find the slow path. You note a fix to improve access.

options.label: Pause new design work and test reliability
options.outcome: You run a basic check on performance and reliability. You confirm the slowdown and log what you see.

episodes.title: Morning Architecture Notes
episodes.text: You sit down at your desk and open your database architecture document. You update the diagrams with yesterday's changes. You write a short note under each change so the structure stays clear.

episodes.title: Talking Through Requirements
episodes.text: You join a video call with a system architect and a design analyst. You listen while they walk through what the business needs next.

choice.prompt: They describe two different business needs at once. What do you clarify first?

options.label: Ask about expected growth and security limits
options.outcome: You write down their numbers and rules. You use them to shape the next design.

options.label: Ask to see the current application flow
options.outcome: They share their screen and walk you through it. You note where the database has to support it.

chat.text: We need the new application to handle more users without slowing down.
Can you talk through what that means for the database structure?
Let's make sure we capture the security needs too before you start.

episodes.title: Planning Efficient Access
episodes.text: You open a quiet design file and sketch how the generic structure will be accessed. You plan where to use an interface, a data transfer step, and data partitions. You check that each piece will allow efficient access without extra work.

trial.title: Spot what needs attention
trial.scenario: You look at your design for efficient access. The interface is clear and the data partitions look right, but the data transfer step keeps timing out in your notes. Users cannot reach the generic structure until it completes.
options: The data transfer mechanism needs attention first
The interface needs attention first
The data partitions need attention first
trial.explain: The transfer step is the one blocking access to the structure.

episodes.title: Afternoon Reliability Check
episodes.text: You open the same database checklist you used yesterday. You go down the list for scalability, security, performance, and reliability. You mark each box the same way, same as yesterday, same tomorrow.

episodes.title: Slow Data Transfer
episodes.text: You get a message that the business application is running slow. You check your design and see the data transfer step is holding everything up. You need to decide how to steady it.

choice.prompt: The application is slow now. What do you do first?

options.label: Redesign the transfer step to be smaller and steadier
options.outcome: You split the transfer into smaller parts. The application steadies while you watch it.

options.label: Add a temporary table to hold the waiting data
options.outcome: You set up a global temporary table for the waiting rows. The application can keep working while you fix the transfer.

options.label: Pause and document what you see before changing anything
options.outcome: You write down the slowdown and what led to it. You share it before you make a change.

episodes.title: Writing It Down
episodes.text: You return to your architecture document. You record today's strategy from modeling through design to implementation. You close the file so tomorrow starts clear.
